title: The whole of it
hookLine: Ananda says good friendship is half the holy life; no, the whole (SN 45.2)

lines: THE FRIEND WHO GETS YOU THERE.
cards: A friend drags someone to the gym on a cold morning. Another says, kindly, that a relationship isn't doing them any good. A third just keeps showing up, again and again, until the other person starts showing up too.
Ananda, the Buddha's attendant, has been thinking about friendship. He comes to the Buddha in a Sakyan town and says, with some confidence, that he's worked out how much good friends are worth.
He's about to be told he's off by half.

teach.h: HALF THE HOLY LIFE, SAYS ANANDA
teach.b: SN 45.2 is short, with a surprise in the middle. Ananda says: half of the holy life, venerable sir, is good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship. A generous estimate.
The Buddha's reply is immediate. Not so, Ananda, not so.

teach.h: NOT SO: THE ENTIRE HOLY LIFE
teach.b: Good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship is the entire holy life.
When someone has a good friend, he explains, you can expect them to develop the noble eightfold path, right view, right intention, all the way through. A good friend doesn't just help with the path.

They're how the path gets walked. Then he points to himself. It's by relying on me as a good friend that beings subject to birth are freed from birth, beings subject to aging, from aging, subject to sorrow, from sorrow.
The teacher calls himself a friend.

teach.h: THE BUDDHA AS A GOOD FRIEND
teach.b: The Pali phrase is kalyanamittata, having a lovely, good friend: kalyana means beautiful, good, and mitta means friend. It doesn't mean someone who agrees with everything.
Another discourse in the Numbered Sayings sketches a good friend as one who speaks up, can bear to be spoken to, and doesn't lead you toward what harms.

Look back at this week: one arrow instead of two, foam on the river, the burden put down, a dog circling its post, tears more than the oceans, a line of mothers with no beginning. Heavy material, most of it.
And the week ends with the Buddha saying the way through all of it is walked with friends.

how: Buddhist communities across traditions practice together in sanghas, temples and retreat groups, and teachers often cite this sutta when they speak about spiritual friendship.

o: a kind spirit who guards your path
a good friend who helps you grow
a friend who always agrees with you

s: the Buddha agrees good friendship is half the holy life
he says not so: it is the entire holy life.
in SN 45.2 the Buddha calls himself a good friend
by relying on him as a good friend, beings are freed from birth, aging and sorrow.
in the texts a good friend is one who agrees with everything
a good friend speaks up, can bear to be spoken to, and doesn't lead you toward harm.

games.q: you're Ananda. you've thought it through and tell the Buddha good friendship is half the holy life. what does he say?
o: not so: it is the entire holy life.
friendship has nothing to do with it.
games.why: he corrects Ananda at once: good friendship is the whole of the holy life, because with a good friend the path gets walked.

practice: Bring to mind one good friend, someone who has helped you become a little kinder, a little braver, and remember one specific time they showed up for you. Let gratitude fill the chest without pushing it.
Then, if you'd like, hold a simple wish for them: may you be well.

wordCard.voice: Kalyanamitta. The Pali term for a good or lovely friend, from SN 45.2, where the Buddha tells Ananda that good friendship is not half but the entire holy life. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali kalyanamitta: a good or lovely friend; kalyanamittata is good friendship.

carryVoice: Your line: walked with friends. Not half the path, the whole of it. That's a week.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 7.37 (Dutiyamitta Sutta), qualities of a good friend
